title: Consumer Response to Chapter 11 Bankruptcy: Negative Demand Spillover to Competitors
authors: O. Cem Ozturk; Pradeep K. Chintagunta; Sriram Venkataraman
eligible_reason: Not a staggered design. Chrysler's Chapter 11 filing (30 Apr 2009) is a single common date for all dealers. The main estimates are dealer-level fixed-effects Poisson models (xtpoisson) of competitor unit sales on the post-filing dummy, with fourth-order daily polynomial trends interacted with post and many time-varying controls (incentives, advertising, inventory, recalls, consumer confidence, Cash-for-Clunkers indicators). They are complemented by regression discontinuity in time (rdrobust) on residualized sales. Web-search regressions use brand dummies and a common post dummy.
design_notes: Replication_Codes_Table_4/5/8/10.do: xtpoisson nsold ... c.post_chfi, fe vce(robust), with model, day-of-month, day-of-week, quarter and end-of-month FE. Table 8 uses weekly post-filing bins, Table 10 interacts post with segment overlap. Table_6/7.do: bootstrapped rdrobust res day_id_c, c(0), uniform/triangular/Epanechnikov kernels. Table_11/12*.do: OLS of web search, parts, bankruptcy and discount search on brand dummies and post_chfi.
screener_notes: Screened from package only. The data appear to be original (non-missing dealer daily unit sales), and the README makes no synthetic-data statement.
